subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt/rebase the open conflicting fork PR, or close/supersede it and queue a fresh narrow same-repo fix for this session-title metadata bug?
rationale: The bug shape is source-reproducible, but an open conflicting fork PR with closing syntax already owns the issue in GitHub linkage, so automation should not create a competing fix until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the stale conflicting fork PR and land a focused same-repo fix that covers metadata stripping, computed displayName precedence, sync and async paths, and proof.

options.title: Adopt/Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer or contributor update the open fork PR against current main and add real TUI/Gateway behavior proof before review.

options.title: Keep Waiting On Fork PR
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the open fork branch despite no updates since April 2026 and a conflicting merge state.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the stale conflicting fork PR and land a focused same-repo fix that covers metadata stripping, computed displayName precedence, sync and async paths, and proof.
